interest: Shows Japan's 1930s South American resource and manufacturing bids, and an Uruguayan diplomat's use of US data against them.
overview: This file comprises State Department records relating to Japanese capital investment and commercial expansion in Latin America—specifically Chile and Uruguay—between January 1933 and December 1934. It opens with a cross-reference sheet to a 1933 Paris despatch from Ambassador Walter E. Edge regarding Japanese participation in the Lonquimay shale oil deposits in Chile, followed by internal State Department memoranda from late 1934 evaluating Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 910. That despatch reported an offer by Japanese manufacturers to establish textile, porcelain, and toy factories in a newly opened free port zone in Uruguay, along with an effort by the skeptical Uruguayan Chargé d'Affaires in Tokyo to obtain U.S. commercial data on Japanese export growth to help defeat the scheme. Officials from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and the Division of Latin-American Affairs (including Maxwell M. Hamilton, Stanley K. Hornbeck, and Joseph F. McGurk) deliberated on the propriety of supplying such information, ultimately recommending that only public commercial data be provided and that any requests for confidential materials follow formal diplomatic channels through Washington or Montevideo.
